meanings.en: sometimes, occasionally, every now and then
meanings.note: Refers to something happening from time to time

examples.trans: I sometimes meet my friend.
It rains occasionally.

같다.gloss: to be like, to be the same

meanings.note: Used after nouns as 같은 to mean 'like a ~'

examples.trans: The weather today is like spring.
We go to the same school.

meanings.note: Compound of 개콘 (short for 개그콘서트, KBS comedy show) + 표 (ticket)

examples.trans: It's really hard to get Gag Concert tickets.

examples.text: 이번 주 개콘표 두 장 있어요?
examples.trans: Do you have two Gag Concert tickets for this week?

meanings.note: Bound noun; commonly shortened to 거 in speech
Used after adnominal verb/adjective endings -(으)ㄴ, -는, -(으)ㄹ

examples.trans: It's something I like.
It's good to go to bed early.

meanings.note: ㅅ-irregular verb (긋다 -> 그어); 선을 긋다 also figuratively means 'to draw a boundary'

examples.trans: I drew a line on the paper.
You have to draw the line from the start.

meanings.note: Often used with 하다 (기대하다 / 기대를 하다)

examples.trans: Expectations for the new movie are high.
Don't have too high expectations.

meanings.note: Plain/informal 1st person singular pronoun; becomes 내가 before subject particle -가

examples.trans: I'll go first.
I want to go together too.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

meanings.note: Formed from 다 (all) + plural suffix -들

examples.trans: Has everyone been doing well?
Everyone, gather over here.

meanings.note: Common colloquial intensifier in spoken Korean

examples.trans: The weather is really cold today.
That food is really delicious.

meanings.note: In -게 되다, means 'to come to / end up doing'

meanings.en: to work, be okay, be allowed
meanings.note: 안 되다 means 'to not work / not be allowed / no'

examples.trans: I came to work here starting tomorrow.
You're not allowed to park here.
See you again tomorrow!
It started raining again.

meanings.note: 또 만나요 is a common farewell meaning 'See you again!'

examples.trans: I met a friend on the weekend.
Let's meet again next week.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.

meanings.note: In -(으)ㄴ/는/단 말이에요, adds emphatic 'I mean / the thing is'

examples.trans: You speak Korean well.
That's not what I mean.

meanings.note: Used both as an adverb and a noun

examples.trans: I drink coffee every morning.
I try to exercise every day.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch, to look

meanings.note: Casual imperative is 봐 (from 보아)

examples.trans: I watched an interesting movie yesterday.
Look closely over here.

meanings.note: Used in 선을 긋다 (to draw the line / set boundaries)

examples.trans: Please do not step outside the line.
I drew a line between work and private life.

meanings.note: Compound of 성적 (grades/results) + 표 (chart/sheet)

examples.trans: I received my report card at school today.
I showed my report card to my parents.

meanings.note: ㅂ-irregular adjective (쉽다 -> 쉬워요)

examples.trans: This problem is really easy.

examples.text: 새로운 언어를 배우는 건 쉽지 않아요.
examples.trans: Learning a new language isn't easy.

meanings.note: Compound of 시청률 (viewership ratings) + 표 (chart/table)

examples.trans: Producers check the ratings chart every morning.

examples.text: 책상 위에 어제 시청률표가 놓여 있어요.
examples.trans: Yesterday's ratings chart is lying on the desk.

meanings.note: Short for 아침밥

examples.trans: I woke up early in the morning.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 요사이

examples.trans: How have you been doing these days?
I have too much work lately.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: 이것이 commonly contracts to 이게 in spoken Korean

examples.trans: What is this?
This is my bag.

meanings.note: Used before time nouns like 이번 주 (this week)

examples.trans: There is a meeting this Friday.
I will definitely succeed this time.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: Used in 이번 주 (this week), 다음 주 (next week)

examples.trans: One week is seven days.
I'm going to go on a trip next week.

meanings.note: 처음부터 means 'from the start'

examples.trans: Let's start over from the beginning.
This is my first time coming to Seoul.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral; used for percentages, dates, phone numbers, and scores

examples.trans: The ratings came out to seven percent.
July is summer.

meanings.note: Present adnominal modifier is 하는

meanings.en: to have, hold (an expectation, thought, etc.)
meanings.note: Used with nouns like 기대를 하다 (to have expectations)

examples.trans: What work are you doing right now?
I exercise every day.

meanings.note: Often used in 혼란이 오다 (to get confused)

examples.trans: I got confused by the sudden change.
The scene fell into great chaos.
